sourceAttempts.result: The official National Paddle Trail page lists 15 established docks, public addresses and river-mile positions from Port Barre through Patterson. Fourteen direct dock-pair/combined itineraries plus ten additional contiguous combinations provide distinct town-to-town reaches from Port Barre through Centerville without inventing access points.
The project describes Bayou Teche as Louisiana's National Water Trail, provides parish maps with safety information, and identifies town-to-town trips generally in the 5–12 mile range.
The basin commission links live USGS streamflow and stage readings at Port Barre, Arnaudville, Adeline Bridge near Jeanerette and Keystone, supporting a monitored corridor conditions check.
USGS 07385450 at Bayou Teche at Port Barre is the direct continuous discharge station used for route scoring; downstream readings should be cross-checked when available.
Coordinates are map-level water-entry anchors geocoded from the official dock addresses and marked for field verification of floating-dock edge, parking and carry path.
Selected Bayou Teche.jpg, a same-river St. Landry Parish photograph by Shane K. Bernard via Wikimedia Commons under CC BY-SA 3.0.

thresholdEvidence.reachApplicability: A conservative screening floor for the monitored Bayou Teche corridor. No official universal runnable band was published; depth, wind-driven reversals, obstructions, traffic, rain and local dock conditions remain decisive.

validation: Focused Bayou Teche route safety test passed.
